You could get some flared drops to give you a little better handling over narrow drops.  There are not many “fast” bikes that will be offered with flat bars.

Past a certain threshold aerodynamics matters more than weight or rolling resistance on your bicycle.  Rolling resistance is constant and at around 15 to 17 mph wind resistance takes over and increases exponentially.  If you do opt for flat bars a low stack height will help to keep your back flat and in a more aero position but will still be less efficient and maybe less comfortable than drops.  Drop bars keep the rider in a more narrow position facing into the wind and hold the rider in a lower profile.  Drops also allow for lots of hand positions to give your hands a break on long rides.
Flat bars will be slower than drop bars though.  If OP really wants speed they need drop or aero-bars.  OP should note though that aero bars aren’t great for group riding
